## Classical baseline

<!-- ~6 lines. Introduce G_0 and G_1, then the two consistency
     equations. Say in one sentence why generating functions are the
     right tool: convolution of component-size distributions becomes
     composition. -->

$$
G_0(x)=\sum_{k\ge 0}P(k)x^k,
\qquad
G_1(x)=\frac{G_0'(x)}{G_0'(1)},
$$ {#eq-gf}

$$
H_1(x) = \bigl(1-p_2\bigr) + p_2\, x\,G_1\!\bigl(H_1(x)\bigr),
\qquad
H_0(x) = x\,G_0\!\bigl(H_1(x)\bigr).
$$ {#eq-h}

<!-- ~4 lines: u = H_1(1) satisfies u = 1 - p_2 + p_2 G_1(u); p_c is the
     smallest p at which a solution u < 1 appears; S = 1 - G_0(u); and
     <s> = H_0'(1) diverges at the transition. -->

## After the $q$-swap

<!-- ~10 lines. Walk the reader through the modification:
     following an edge into a degree-q node on which a q-swap was
     performed, one no longer reaches a q-1 star but a q-cycle whose
     links have SCP p (not p_2). Summing over the length l of the
     connected string of vertices reached inside the cycle gives C_q(x),
     Eq. (2) of the paper; H~_1 then picks up one term per active
     q-swap, Eq. (3). Reproduce both. Then state the detaching
     correction in H~_0 and the definition of beta_q (probability that
     no neighbouring q'-swap was performed), including the compact
     single-type approximation beta_q ~ [1 + q P_1(q)/2]^{-1}. -->

$$
\tilde H_1(x) = 1-p_2 + p_2\,x\,G_1\!\bigl(\tilde H_1(x)\bigr)
+ \sum_{q\ge 2}\gamma_q\,\tilde H_{1,q}(x).
$$ {#eq-h1tilde}

<!-- Follow with H~_{1,q}(x) and C_q(x). Then: -->

$$
\tilde H_0(x) = x\,G_0\!\bigl(\tilde H_1(x)\bigr)
+ x\sum_{q\ge2}\gamma_q\beta_q P(q)\Bigl\{1-\bigl[\tilde H_1(x)\bigr]^q\Bigr\},
\qquad
\tilde S = 1-\tilde H_0(1).
$$ {#eq-stilde}
